reasons: y puts the new Gateway backend client certificate feature in its own file, backend_client_certificate.go, so the file boundary matches the feature boundary. x adds resolveBackendClientCertificate, makeGatewayResolvedRefsCondition and gatewayResolvedRefsCondition to kubernetes.go, which is already over 2,300 lines.

y keeps the request-mirror code together in httproute.go: loadHTTPRouteRequestMirror and httpRouteRequestMirrorRatio sit next to loadMiddlewares, and mirror backends are staged in mirrorConf. x adds a separate func type, mirrorServiceLoader, with a factory, newMirrorServiceLoader, and passes the closure through loadMiddlewares and loadService. This adds indirection and puts the mirror logic in two places.

y's buildHTTPRouteRetry is a plain function placed next to loadHTTPRouteConfiguration, its only caller. x's createRetry is a Provider method among the stateless create* builders, so it is the odd one out in that group.

x has a structural advantage: it passes the client certificate into loadServersTransport and loadTCPServersTransport, so all ServersTransport TLS setup stays in one builder. y attaches BackendClientCertificates afterwards in three places: loadHTTPServers, loadGRPCServers and loadTLSServers. This advantage does not outweigh y's cleaner file layout.

In y, the client certificate is passed into loadServersTransport (httproute.go) and loadTCPServersTransport (tlsroute.go), where the ServersTransport is built. x instead repeats a `serversTransport.Certificates = listener.BackendClientCertificates` assignment after the policy loop in loadHTTPServers, loadGRPCServers and loadTLSServers, so the same feature logic is spread across three route files.

y places resolveBackendClientCertificate in kubernetes.go next to resolveFrontendValidation and resolveCACertificateRefs, which follows how the package already handles Gateway-level TLS references. x's new backend_client_certificate.go is a clean feature file, but it breaks that pattern while its tests remain in kubernetes_test.go.

y moves the Gateway ResolvedRefs decision out of makeGatewayStatus into gatewayResolvedRefsCondition and makeGatewayResolvedRefsCondition, so each job has its own helper. x adds one more branch to the switch inside the already long makeGatewayStatus.

y's mirrorServiceLoader type lets loadMiddlewares stay focused on filters: it no longer needs the gateway, listener or statusReport parameters. x passes all of that through loadMiddlewares, adds a temporary mirrorConf merge inside it, and keeps loadHTTPRouteRequestMirror as a separate Provider method.

y puts the builders createRequestMirror and mirrorRatio next to the other create* filter builders in httproute.go. x adds cross-file coupling comments in the Provider and gatewayListener structs ("read by httproute.go..."), which shows the boundaries are leaking.

y puts resolveBackendClientCertificate in kubernetes.go next to resolveFrontendValidation and resolveCACertificateRefs. Gateway-level TLS reference resolution was already grouped there. x moves only this one resolver into a new backend_client_certificate.go, which splits a group of related resolvers.

In y, the retry and mirror middlewares are pure builders, createHTTPRouteRetry and createHTTPRouteRequestMirror. They sit with createCORS, createURLRewrite and createRequestRedirect in httproute.go, which follows the existing filter-builder pattern. In x, buildHTTPRouteRetry sits between loadHTTPRouteConfiguration and loadWRRService, and its build* prefix puts it with the rule builders (buildMatchRule, buildPathRule).

x splits the mirror filter into a Provider method, loadHTTPRouteRequestMirror, plus httpRouteRequestMirrorRatio. It also adds a mirrorConf staging configuration to loadMiddlewares. That spreads one filter across three places. y loads the mirror backend inline in loadMiddlewares and keeps the middleware construction in a single create* function.

y's gatewayListener.BackendClientCertificate is a single *tls.Certificate, set the same way as the other per-listener fields. x adds a comment to the Provider struct saying the field 'is read by httproute.go', which ties the struct to the files that use it.

y's makeGatewayStatus builds the ResolvedRefs condition once and then overrides it. The backend certificate condition fits into that existing status flow, and Test_resolveBackendClientCertificate unit-tests the resolver next to Test_resolveFrontendValidation.

y puts the new Gateway backend client certificate feature in its own file, backend_client_certificate.go (loadBackendClientCertificate plus newBackendClientCertificateCondition), so the file boundary matches the feature boundary. x adds resolveBackendClientCertificate to kubernetes.go, which is already a 2,300-line catch-all.

In y, the four condition literals that x repeats inside resolveBackendClientCertificate become one helper, newBackendClientCertificateCondition, so the certificate-reference logic stays compact and in one place.

y gives the request-mirror filter one method of its own in httproute.go, loadHTTPRouteRequestMirror, with a pure helper httpRouteRequestMirrorRatio. x splits the same filter between an inline block in loadMiddlewares and createHTTPRouteRequestMirror.

x's createHTTPRouteRetry and createHTTPRouteRequestMirror match the existing create* builders in httproute.go and keep loadMiddlewares simpler. y adds mirrorConf staging inside loadMiddlewares, which makes that function more complex.

Both thread the certificate through gatewayListener into grpcroute.go, httproute.go and tlsroute.go the same way. y's field, BackendClientCertificates of type tls.Certificates, assigns directly without a nil check, but its makeGatewayStatus puts the new condition argument in the middle of the parameter list.

Backend client certificate: x passes the certificate into the transport builders, `loadServersTransport` in httproute.go (shared by HTTP and gRPC) and `loadTCPServersTransport` in tlsroute.go. That keeps the logic in the code that builds the transport. y repeats the same post-loop patch three times, in `loadHTTPServers`, `loadGRPCServers` and `loadTLSServers`.

Gateway ResolvedRefs: in kubernetes.go, x gives this its own functions, `gatewayResolvedRefsCondition` and `makeGatewayResolvedRefsCondition`, and `resolveBackendClientCertificate` reuses the helper. y writes the condition inline inside `makeGatewayStatus` and repeats the full condition literal three times in `resolveBackendClientCertificate`.

Request mirror: x gives `loadMiddlewares` a small `mirrorServiceLoader` type, so the filter-to-middleware code does not need to know about gateways or listeners, and the ratio math sits in its own `mirrorRatio`. y widens the `loadMiddlewares` signature with gatewayName, listener, route and statusReport, which ties middleware building to service loading.

Retry is the one point in y's favour: y's free function `createHTTPRouteRetry` matches the other `create*` builders better than x's `Provider.createRetry` method. It is too small to change the overall result.

Backend client certificate: y passes it into loadServersTransport (httproute.go) and loadTCPServersTransport (tlsroute.go), so all the code that builds the transport is in one place. x adds the same 'if serversTransport != nil && listener.BackendClientCertificate != nil' block after loading in loadHTTPServers, loadGRPCServers and loadTLSServers.

Gateway ResolvedRefs: in y's kubernetes.go, the condition logic lives in gatewayResolvedRefsCondition and makeGatewayResolvedRefsCondition, which resolveBackendClientCertificate and makeGatewayStatus reuse. x writes the condition structs out inline in both functions and adds a switch inside makeGatewayStatus.

Request mirror: y's mirrorServiceLoader type narrows loadMiddlewares to filter work (namespace, parent name, filters, loader). x makes loadMiddlewares take gateway name and namespace, listener, route and statusReport only so it can call loadService for mirrors, which couples filter loading to backend loading.

y splits the mirror ratio math into mirrorRatio, apart from building the middleware in createRequestMirror, and builds the retry middleware once per rule. x keeps both inside the per-match loop and in a single createHTTPRouteRetry/createHTTPRouteRequestMirror pair.

x's gatewayListener.BackendClientCertificate comment names httproute.go, grpcroute.go and tlsroute.go as the places that read it, which shows the feature is spread across files instead of sitting behind one owner.
